scene-u01-pnew1-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 12 · KP01 When neighboring observations are not independent

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Point-by-point decisions are fooled by the ambiguous second observation; sequence decisions also count the class order

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: the left shows likelihoods at three positions; the right compares labels picked by the two decisions; the table multiplies fit $\times$ plausibility into a sequence score.

scene-u01-pnew1-58.name: text#58
scene-u01-pnew1-58.text: "It just averages point answers" is wrong: it can overturn better-looking answers.

scene-u01-pnew1-85.name: text#85
scene-u01-pnew1-85.text: Both factors are below $1$ and the score is a product; switching twice in $\omega_1\omega_2\omega_1$ leaves plausibility only $0.005$.

scene-u01-pnew1-87.name: text#87
scene-u01-pnew1-87.text: Example: likelihoods and stay probability $0.9$ are added

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 12 · KP01 When neighboring observations are not independent

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: One label depends on three things: its own value, neighboring values, and the order of classes

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the bottom row is observations, the top row labels; blue lines are own values, green lines neighboring values, purple arrows label order; the glowing $\omega_{i_3}$ is the one to decide.

scene-u01-pnew2-49.name: text#49
scene-u01-pnew2-49.text: Isolated classification uses only the blue line; this chapter adds green and purple, so the unit of classification becomes a whole sequence.

scene-u01-pnew2-66.name: text#66
scene-u01-pnew2-66.text: Which class tends to follow which

scene-u01-pnew2-81.name: text#81
scene-u01-pnew2-81.text: Neighboring pixels often share a region

scene-u01-pnew2-85.name: text#85
scene-u01-pnew2-85.text: "Dependence is just extra noise" is wrong: correlation is information, and order patterns are clues for correcting errors. Isolated classification wastes it.

scene-u01-pnew3-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 12 · KP01 When neighboring observations are not independent

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Dependence need not be strong: once the stay probability exceeds about $0.525$, the sequence decision overturns the point answer

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the horizontal axis is the stay probability $p$, the vertical axis the score ratio of two candidates; the red dashed line is $1$ (equal); the right table computes three values of $p$.

scene-u01-pnew3-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew3-8.text: Score ratio: best sequence vs point answer

scene-u01-pnew3-28.name: text#28
scene-u01-pnew3-28.text: Vertical: score of $\omega_1\omega_1\omega_1$ $\div$ score of $\omega_1\omega_2\omega_1$ (log scale, $10\times$ per grid line)

scene-u01-pnew3-69.name: text#69
scene-u01-pnew3-69.text: The fit ratio $0.324/0.396=0.818$ must be made up by the plausibility ratio $\big(p/(1-p)\big)^2$; setting the product to $1$ gives $p^*\approx0.525$. [Added] At $p=0.5$ there is no order information and the sequence decision falls back to the point answer.
